solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hill-climbing traveller?

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters go upwards, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Damon Hill, the Formula One world champion, so Hill gives his first name, DAMON

explanation.surface: A hiker scaling a hill is a kind of traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill' looks like a slope to climb, but it is the racing driver Damon Hill; his first name reads upwards ('climbing') in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home, a traveller by way of life.

clue.text: Pay money to bandage inflamed hair fracture

indicators.note: to bandage is to wrap round, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to pay money is to spend
inflamed means set alight, lit

explanation.surface: Someone pays to have an inflamed hairline crack in a bone bandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair fracture' sounds like a hairline crack in bone; read literally it is a broken hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A split end is a strand of hair that has frayed and broken apart at its tip.

clue.text: Cathar chieftain kidnapping Sussex lad

indicators.note: kidnapping means the two words hold the answer captive within them

explanation.surface: A medieval heretic leader abducts a boy from Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Archie is the son of Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Harry's son Archie is the child of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, hence a boy of that title.

clue.text: Pull in finally in London?

parts.note: to pull a vehicle along is to tow it

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word in

explanation.surface: A vehicle stops at last somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: To Londoners, 'town' means central London, as in 'going up to town'; the question mark marks London as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: London is a town, and in British usage 'town' often means the capital itself.

clue.text: Irish county's banning golf forever

indicators.note: banning means shutting the letter out of the word

parts.note: Galway is a county in the west of Ireland; with the 's it gives GALWAYS
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Irish county has banned golf for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Always and forever both mean at all times, without end.

clue.text: Log rolling — ready kids?

indicators.note: rolling suggests tumbling over and over, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Children ready for a log-rolling game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log rolling' looks like a lumberjack sport; 'Log' is the definition and 'rolling' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk diary is a book for recording appointments and events, a kind of log.

clue.text: Breaking news: Spooner — poor chap — stripped of his status

indicators.note: breaking into the two letters means the jumbled name goes between them

parts.note: N is new, so news, two of them, gives NN

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A news flash reports that the Reverend Spooner, poor fellow, has been defrocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' puts the jumbled name inside the two Ns, and 'poor' is the anagram signal. 'Spooner' suggests a spoonerism, but there is none: the name is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonperson is someone treated as having no rights or existence, a man whose standing has been removed.

clue.text: Foreign film

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means strange or foreign

explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or strange, and Alien is a famous film.

clue.text: Motorway's boring eyesore spoiling green strategy

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the road goes inside the eyesore

parts.note: a stye is literally a sore on the eyelid
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; read as MI

explanation.surface: A motorway carving through the countryside is an eyesore ruining plans for the green belt.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, a stymie was a ball blocking another's line to the hole on the putting green. 'Motorway' is the M1, the London-to-Leeds motorway, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: In old golf rules a stymie was an opponent's ball in the way of your putt, wrecking your plan on the green.

clue.text: Undesirable pub song penned

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so the song goes inside the pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: An unpleasant song has been written about a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like 'written', but here means enclosed. 'Undesirable' is a noun here: an undesirable person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is a social outcast, someone shunned as unwanted.

clue.text: Pass made by S. Spielberg's favourite actor after new Oscar

indicators.note: after says the actor's name follows the two letters

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Steven Spielberg's favourite actor is reputedly Tom Hanks, written T. Hanks to match the initial S.

explanation.surface: An actor much loved by Spielberg wins an Oscar, then declines a role.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S.' initial invites 'T. Hanks' for Tom Hanks, giving THANKS whole. 'made by' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I'll pass' politely declines an offer, just as the phrase does.

clue.text: Jilt Juliet in Crete when sozzled

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet dumps her lover after getting drunk on a Cretan holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes in CRETE ('in') and 'when sozzled' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To jilt someone is to cast them off as a partner, a romantic rejection.

clue.text: Husband wearing cravat. Loud. Criminal, actually

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the letter sits inside the neckwear

parts.note: a cravat is a kind of tie
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A husband in a flashy cravat turns out to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actually' only adds emphasis to the surface and links.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is one kind of criminal, someone who steals.

clue.text: Neat, if simple retro housing eccentric

indicators.note: retro says the hidden letters are read backwards
housing means the phrase holds the letters within it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tidy but plain retro-styled home for an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'housing' in the definition; it is the hiding signal, leaving 'eccentric' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is someone who does not fit in, an oddball or eccentric.

clue.text: Wearing short dungarees to work, question artiste

indicators.note: the question letter wears the scrambled garment, so it sits inside
to work means the letters are worked over into a new order
short means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone in shortened dungarees for work asks about a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts DUNGAREES to DUNGAREE, 'to work' rearranges it, and 'Wearing' puts Q inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag queen is a performer, typically a man, who entertains in flamboyant women's dress.

clue.text: Good, free crossword?

parts.note: to free is to rid

explanation.surface: A good crossword that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a part for the whole: the grid is the crossword's frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is built on a grid of squares, so the grid can stand for the puzzle.

clue.text: Send abroad fabric — tons leaving repeatedly

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the word

parts.note: a fabric is a textile

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter is taken twice

explanation.surface: Cloth is exported abroad, with tons shipped out again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ts leave TEXTILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their own country.

clue.text: Real adversity oddly bypassed first-born

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are skipped, so the even ones remain

explanation.surface: The first child got through real hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child is the one born first in a family.

clue.text: Former president familiarly ignoring bill for sailing ship

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving these letters out of the name

parts.note: Barack Obama, the former US president, called by his first name
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Obama skips paying the bill for a sailing trip.
explanation.walkthrough: BARK is the less common spelling of barque, a sailing ship with three or more masts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bark, or barque, is a type of sailing vessel with several masts.

clue.text: When ordering hotel tables, wife's admitted in the cheap seats?

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the letter goes inside
ordering means putting into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife gets let in while hotel tables are booked.
explanation.walkthrough: At old banquets the salt cellar marked the divide: lesser guests sat below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the salt means seated among the lower-ranking guests, far from the host's end of the table.

clue.text: Adult sin? I think so, too

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being grown up is sinful, and another concurs.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Agreed' is said to show concurrence, sharing someone's opinion.

clue.text: Shun key hospital we set up

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means placed upwards, so the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: We were told to avoid the key hospital we founded.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to avoid or abstain from it deliberately.

clue.text: Elmer left base to go on a bender

parts.note: Elmer Fudd is the cartoon hunter who chases Bugs Bunny
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A man named Elmer quit his military base to binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuddle as a verb, rare now, means to drink heavily, to booze until muddled.

clue.text: Frank Capra for one robbed of gold

indicators.note: robbed of means the metal is taken out of the word

parts.note: Frank Capra was a Hollywood film director, an example of one
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: The film-maker Frank Capra has had his gold stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' is not Capra's first name here but the definition, meaning blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct and frank both describe speech that is straightforward and honest.

clue.text: 500! Five hundred sheets! Imagine!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a ream of paper is 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Exclamations of surprise at an order of 500 sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream of something is to imagine or fantasise it.

clue.text: Striking actors start to sabotage The Vanquished

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
the actors in a production are its cast

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Actors on strike begin to undermine a film called The Vanquished.
explanation.walkthrough: This answer names the theme: other answers are outcasts too.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcasts are people driven out and rejected, as the defeated often are.

clue.text: See 18
Benefit one writing cheque returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the drawer of a cheque is the person who writes and signs it

explanation.surface: A payout from someone whose cheque bounced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' sounds like a bounced cheque, but it reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a benefit or return for something done.

clue.text: Article dropped by someone jumping — he's untouchable

indicators.note: dropped by means the letter is let go from the word

parts.note: a leaper is someone who jumps
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A jumper sheds his kit and becomes unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untouchable' suggests unbeatable, but means one shunned for fear of contagion.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper was historically shunned, someone people refused to touch for fear of infection.

clue.text: Bath's no.1 forward Thiebaud regularly getting sent off, the idiot

indicators.note: no.1 picks the opening letter of the team's name

parts.note: a lock is a forward in rugby union

indicators.note: every other letter is sent off, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Bath's star rugby forward Thiebaud keeps being sent off, the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English rugby union club; a lock is a second-row forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead is a stupid person, a dolt.
